title: cohort-fenced-swap-with-rollback-replay-and-telemetry
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a cohort-fenced model swap flow that provides session-consistent handover, automated rollback-replay for failing cohorts, and enhanced telemetry for per-cohort diagnostics. This PR introduces a new lifecycle controller component (cohort-fence controller), small runtime hooks to enforce session affinity during swaps, and a replay pipeline that captures request traces and payloads for repro.

Motivation and context: Customers running staged rollouts (canary, shadow, A/B) need deterministic semantics when a cohort is promoted or rolled back. Previously, partial traffic swaps could split sessions mid-flight (user experiences multiple model versions within a session) making debugging and quality validation difficult. In a recent incident (SUP-5123) we observed hard-to-reproduce regressions because rollback lacked deterministic replay for affected cohorts. This work implements three capabilities: (1) cohort fencing to guarantee session-consistent swapping, (2) an automated rollback-replay that replays captured cohort traffic against a candidate model snapshot, and (3) per-cohort telemetry (latency, token-cost, quality delta) surfaced to Console and to tracing backends.

Design highlights: - Cohort fence: a lightweight lease attached to routing metadata. When a cohort swap is initiated, the controller sets a fence lease and the router will maintain session affinity for the duration of the lease (configurable TTL). The fence improves safety for small, stateful cohorts and prevents split-session exposure during drain.
- Rollback-replay pipeline: on detection of safety gate violations (latency or quality thresholds), the controller marks cohort traffic for capture (sampling by cohort). Captured traces are stored in an encrypted replay bucket with metadata linking to the model build hash. A replay worker can then re-run requests against the previous model binary to reproduce the regression and produce a diff report.
- Telemetry: added cohort-level metrics (cohort.latency.p50/p95, cohort.token_cost.avg, cohort.quality.delta) and tracing spans that propagate model version and cohort_id. Console dashboards and SLO rules can now reference cohort.* metrics.

Checklist: - [x] Cohort fence controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Router affinity hooks and TTL enforcement - [x] Rollback capture and replay worker + e2e test harness - [x] Telemetry metrics + traces + Console dashboard wiring - [x] Migration docs and configuration defaults - [x] Performance benchmarks and microbench for router path

Small illustrative snippet (router lease check):

if fenceLease != nil && time.Now().Before(fenceLease.ExpiresAt) {
    // Preserve session affinity to original model until lease expiration
    chosenModel = fenceLease.ModelHash
} else {
    chosenModel = chooseByTrafficSplit(req)
}

CI history: - Initial run (2026-02-17): test/integration failed (capture e2e flake due to ephemeral S3 stub) - Fix pushed (2026-02-18): added S3 stub retry and local buffer fallback - Re-run (2026-02-19): all tests passed on linux/amd64 matrix - Final run (2026-02-22): CI green across all matrices (unit, integration, linters).

Backward compatibility and migration notes: - Default TTL for cohort fence is conservative (30s) to avoid long-lived session pins; customers can tune via rollout policy. - Rollout objects that opt-in to capture must explicitly set capture: true; no existing rollouts are changed by default. - Replay artifacts are encrypted and retained per org retention policy (default 7 days).

Performance: Microbench results included in PR show router path overhead ~0.9% p50 and p95 increase under 99th percentile traffic profiles. Capturing path adds measurable I/O but is gated by sampling and cohort opt-in. Bench outputs attached to the PR artifacts.

How to test locally: - Start local rollout controller: make run-controller - Apply sample rollout with cohort fence enabled: kubectl apply -f examples/cohort_swap.yaml - Trigger a swap and observe cohort.* metrics in prometheus-local and trace spans in Jaeger-local. - Run replay CLI against captured bucket: tools/replay/cli.py replay --cohort-id <id> --model-hash <hash>

Migration docs: docs/rollouts/cohort-fence.md contains configuration knobs, examples for A/B and canary flows, and operator playbook for handling captured artifacts and replay analysis.
